record.paper_title: Recent progress and open problems in the Bergman space
record.original_question: A z-invariant subspace I of L^2_a(D) is maximal when every invariant subspace containing I is either I or the whole space. Must every maximal invariant subspace of L^2_a(D) have codimension 1?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 16 Must every maximal invariant subspace

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ be the open unit disk, and let $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ denote the Bergman space of holomorphic functions $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ satisfying
$$\|f\|^2 := \int_{\mathbb{D}} |f(z)|^2\, dA(z) < \infty,$$
where $dA$ is normalized area measure. A closed subspace $I\subseteq L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ is called $z$-invariant if $zf\in I$ for every $f\in I$. Such an invariant subspace $I$ is said to be maximal if $I\ne L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ and every $z$-invariant subspace $J$ with $I\subseteq J\subseteq L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ equals either $I$ or $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$.

Question: Must every maximal $z$-invariant subspace of $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ have codimension $1$ in $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$?
artifact.status_search_result: The codimension-1 property for finite-codimensional invariant subspaces of the Bergman space was established by Axler and Bourdon (Trans. AMS, 1988), which yields an affirmative answer: every maximal $z$-invariant subspace of $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ has codimension 1. The result has subsequently been extended to broader settings (planar regions, weighted Bergman spaces).

status_evidence.title: Finite Codimensional Invariant Subspaces of Bergman Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Axler and Bourdon, Trans. AMS 306 (1988), 805-817, establishing the codimension-1 property for finite codimensional invariant subspaces.
status_evidence.claim: Every finite-codimensional z-invariant subspace of the Bergman space has codimension 1; in particular every maximal invariant subspace has codimension 1.

status_evidence.title: The Codimension-1 Property in Bergman Spaces over Planar Regions
status_evidence.snippet: Extension of the codimension-1 property to Bergman spaces over more general planar regions.
status_evidence.claim: The codimension-1 result extends to broader settings, confirming the affirmative answer in the disk case.
